opening.text: Here we slow down and read John 3:16 with the two verses that follow: God so loved the world that he gave his Son, he sent him to save and not to judge, and whoever believes in him is not judged.

pieces.heading: Wonder at a love this large
pieces.summary: Matthew Henry asks us to stop and wonder: the holy God loves a wicked world. And this love is not for one nation only. Christ came in love to the whole world, Gentiles as well as Jews.

pieces.heading: Given for ungrateful slaves
pieces.summary: Chrysostom measures this love by the gift. The Father gave his Son for slaves, and ungrateful ones. A man would hardly die even for a friend or a righteous man.

bridge.text: The next verse says why the Father sent the Son into the world.

pieces.heading: The physician who came to heal
pieces.summary: Augustine pictures Christ as a physician. He came to heal the sick, not to judge them. The one who will not follow the physician's orders destroys himself.

bridge.text: The Son came to save the world, so what of the one who believes in him?

pieces.heading: Not condemned: more than a reprieve
pieces.summary: Matthew Henry says the believer is not condemned. A sinner, even a great one, who believes is not just let off for now. He is acquitted and set free, not dealt with as his sins deserve.

rabbi_road.text: Romans 5:8 says the same love another way. God shows his love in this: Christ died for us while we were still sinners. John 3:16 tells us God gave his Son; Romans 5:8 tells us when, before we had done anything to deserve it. Matthew Henry says God commends his love the way a merchant commends his goods, setting it out for us to see and take.
rabbi_road.prompt: God showed his love while we were still sinners. How does that change the way you come to him today?

over_the_hill.text: One hop further, Jesus himself tells us what the greatest love looks like: someone lays down his life for his friends. The love of John 3:16 does not stay far off. It calls us his friends.
